clue.text: Complaint following proposal — still you don't get it!

definitions.note: a playful definition: the condition is one you avoid when you keep still

indicators.note: the word for complaint comes after the word for proposal, so it is placed second

parts.note: a motion is a proposal put to a meeting for debate
a complaint is an illness or ailment

explanation.surface: Someone's marriage proposal is followed by a grumble, and the exasperated speaker says the other person still doesn't understand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complaint' looks like the definition but is half the wordplay; the definition is the joke at the end, since travel sickness strikes only when you are moving.
explanation.definitionFit: Travel nausea is caused by movement, so a person who keeps still never suffers from it.

clue.text: Such a vile man, I'm involved in this?

definitions.text: Such a vile man, I'm involved in this?

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so these letters are twisted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged
taken as written, completing the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A rhetorical question: could such a nasty man as me really be mixed up in this?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the anagram and the definition: the rearranged letters spell an attitude, and a vile man would indeed be wrapped up in it.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the sexist attitude of a man who believes in male superiority, the kind of view a vile man holds.

clue.text: Divergent line of thought, singularly touching

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a straight line touching a curve at exactly one point

explanation.walkthrough: 'Singularly touching' sounds like 'uniquely moving', but here it means touching at a single point, which is what this geometric line does.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry the line meets a curve at one point only, and in talk it is a sudden digression from the subject.

clue.text: Partial judgment, with court supporting old writer and composer

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits underneath, so the court abbreviation goes at the end

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument, so a writer
Giuseppe Verdi, the Italian opera composer

explanation.surface: A judgment that is only partial is handed down, with a court backing an old author and a musician.
explanation.walkthrough: In a coroner's court this verdict records a death without deciding its cause, so it is only a partial judgment.
explanation.definitionFit: This inquest finding confirms a death but leaves the cause undetermined, so the ruling is incomplete.

clue.text: Colonise area taken from Pacific port

indicators.note: taken from means removed out of the port's name, so the abbreviation for area is dropped

parts.note: Seattle is a port city on the Pacific coast of Washington State

explanation.surface: Instructions to colonise an area seized from a Pacific harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: To colonise a land is to go and populate it, which is to set up home there as pioneers.

clue.text: Crazed demoniac who wants to slay people?

definitions.note: to slay an audience is slang for making it laugh helplessly

indicators.note: crazed means driven mad, so the letters of the next word are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A maddened demon-possessed figure who is eager to kill people.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface paints a murderer, but 'slay' is showbiz slang for making an audience helpless with laughter.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand-up performer hopes to slay the crowd, meaning to have them roaring with laughter.

clue.text: Sister, in turn, ignoring the odds

indicators.note: ignoring the odds means skipping the first, third and fifth letters and keeping only the even-placed ones

parts.note: taken as written, the phrase whose even letters are kept

explanation.surface: A sister takes her turn while defying the odds stacked against her.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman in a religious order is addressed as Sister, so the title stands for her.

clue.text: Finishes off in state — is one in Victoria, perhaps?

indicators.note: finishes off means its last letter is cut away

parts.note: taken as written before it is cut
the Roman numeral for one
on can mean in, as in being on the team

explanation.surface: Someone finishing their days in grand style wonders whether they are one of those in Victoria.
explanation.walkthrough: Victoria is a London railway terminus, so 'perhaps' marks it as one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Victoria is one of London's main railway terminals, an example of a place where trains stop.

clue.text: In error, get date wrong? Questioned again

indicators.note: getting something wrong muddles it, so all these letters are reshuffled

parts.note: taken as written, part of the letters to be rearranged
taken as written, the rest of the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A witness asks whether getting a date mistaken is a reason to be grilled once more.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is the past tense of quizzing someone formally for a second time, as police do with a suspect.

clue.text: Mild European imprisoned by famous Communist despot, ultimately

indicators.note: imprisoned by means held inside the Communist leader's name

parts.note: Lenin, leader of the Russian Revolution

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of despot

parts.note: the word whose last letter is taken

explanation.surface: A gentle European is locked up by a notorious Communist tyrant in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Lenient treatment is gentle and forgiving, the opposite of harsh, much as a mild punishment is.

clue.text: Worker gets specific day in charge

parts.note: a man can mean a worker or employee, as in men on the factory floor
a date is a particular day in the calendar

explanation.surface: An employee is given a particular day on which to be in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandate is an official commission or instruction, which is what a charge laid on someone is.

clue.text: Orderly waiters heard signal to act

indicators.note: heard means the word is taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: a queue is a line of people waiting in order

explanation.surface: Tidy restaurant staff pick up a signal that it is time to take action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Waiters' suggests restaurant staff, but here they are simply people waiting in line.
explanation.definitionFit: On stage the cue is the word or action telling an actor to speak or enter.

clue.text: Farewell, in a manner of speaking, after very short drink

indicators.note: the manner of speaking comes after the very short drink in the answer

parts.note: V is the shortened form of very
ale is beer
diction is a person's way of pronouncing words

explanation.surface: A goodbye, as it were, following a quick swift drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a manner of speaking' reads like the idiom for 'so to speak', but it supplies the word for enunciation.
explanation.definitionFit: A valediction is a speech or word of leave-taking, a formal goodbye.

clue.text: Set piece's musical quality in foundational part

parts.note: a corner kick is a set piece in football; with the apostrophe s it gives the possessive
tone is the quality of a musical sound

explanation.surface: A dramatic set piece's musical character lies in its basic underlying section.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set piece' suggests a staged musical number, but it is the football term for a dead-ball kick such as a corner.
explanation.definitionFit: The stone laid at a building's corner is its base, and figuratively the essential element on which something rests.

clue.text: Run after a tyre burst in main road

indicators.note: the run comes after the word a

parts.note: taken as written
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

indicators.note: a burst tyre is blown apart, so its letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A car runs on after a blowout on a major highway.
explanation.definitionFit: An artery is a major route for traffic, likened to the blood vessel carrying the main flow.

clue.text: Spike securing small flier for writer

indicators.note: securing means holding something inside, so the bird goes within the spike

parts.note: a lance is a long pointed weapon

indicators.note: small here means made shorter, so the bird's name loses its last letter

parts.note: a wren is a tiny bird, so a flier

explanation.surface: A spike pins down a little bird to keep it for an author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small' looks like it simply describes the bird, but it tells you to shorten its name by a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: D. H. Lawrence, the English novelist, and T. E. Lawrence, who wrote Seven Pillars of Wisdom, are both authors.

clue.text: Like winner of cup, left after dinner, holding book

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the book's letter sits inside

parts.note: food still on the plate after the meal is uneaten

explanation.surface: A cup-winning side's leftovers from the celebration dinner include a book.
explanation.walkthrough: A knockout cup is won by a team that loses no match, so the winner is undefeated.
explanation.definitionFit: A knockout cup winner loses no tie on the way, so the team ends the competition undefeated.

clue.text: Disturbed over sins, of which the Bible has many

definitions.text: of which the Bible has many

indicators.note: disturbed means thrown into disorder, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone troubled by their wrongdoings turns to scripture, which has plenty to say about them.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bible exists in many translations, such as the King James and the New International.

clue.text: Ill-feeling concealed by veteran courageously

indicators.note: concealed by means the answer lies tucked inside these words

parts.note: the answer runs across the end of veteran and the start of courageously

explanation.surface: An old soldier bravely hides his bitterness.
explanation.definitionFit: Rancour is deep bitter resentment, a long-held hostility toward someone.

clue.text: It contains accounts from sides straddling border

indicators.note: straddling means sitting on either side, so the two sides go around the border

parts.note: left and right, L and R
an edge is a border or rim

explanation.surface: A book of records drawn from both sides of a frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: A ledger is the book in which a business keeps its financial records.

clue.text: Great scientist, person frequently imprisoned — upset one Pope

indicators.note: upset means turned over, which in a down clue reads the word upwards

parts.note: an old lag is a habitual convict
the Roman numeral for one
Leo is the name of many popes

explanation.surface: A great scientist, often jailed, offends a pontiff.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface nods to history: this astronomer was tried by the Church and kept under house arrest. A lag is British slang for a convict.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian astronomer championed the Sun-centred model and is counted among history's greatest scientists.

clue.text: Scoundrel's wife, supporter of school board

definitions.note: read as 'scoundrel is', so the definition is the word scoundrel

parts.note: an easel holds up a blackboard in a classroom

explanation.surface: A rogue's wife sits on a school's governing board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'School board' suggests governors, but it is a classroom blackboard, and its supporter is the stand it rests on.
explanation.definitionFit: A weasel is a sly, untrustworthy person, a common figurative term for a rogue.

clue.text: No point including girl's name, in spite of that

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: including means holding the name inside

parts.note: a ness is a headland or promontory, a point of land
Ethel is a female name

explanation.surface: There is no point mentioning a girl's name, despite that.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means 'however' or 'even so', conceding a point but carrying on.

clue.text: Part of field in cricket match set back

indicators.note: set back means reversed, so the word is written backwards

parts.note: to gel is to go together or match well

explanation.surface: A section of a cricket field where a match has been delayed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Match' suggests the cricket game, but it is the verb meaning to fit together.
explanation.definitionFit: The leg side is the half of a cricket field behind the batsman's legs, also called on side.

clue.text: Angry call about the players, initially, in this event

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shout goes around the initials

parts.note: a shout is a loud cry, often in anger

indicators.note: initially means taking the first letters of these words

parts.note: the first letters of the and players

explanation.surface: An angry yell surrounds the athletes at the start of this competition.
explanation.definitionFit: Hurling a heavy metal ball is an athletics field event.

clue.text: Foreign breed over in Melbourne, say

definitions.meaning: first meaning: short for Pomeranian, a dog breed from Pomerania in north-central Europe
second meaning: Australian slang for a Briton who has come over to live there

explanation.walkthrough: Australians call a British immigrant a Pom, so someone come over to Melbourne is one; the same short word is a toy dog.
explanation.definitionFit: The short word is both a toy dog's nickname and an Australian slang term for an English person.

clue.text: List operations going the wrong way, easily seen in theatre

indicators.note: going the wrong way means read backwards

parts.note: to list is to lean or tilt, as a ship does
ops is a common short form of operations, as in military ops

explanation.surface: A list of procedures run backwards on stage would be plain to spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'List' looks like a noun for a roster, but it is the verb for a ship leaning over.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer picked out by a stage beam is conspicuous to the audience, lit by a focused lamp.

clue.text: Form in which a person's convictions are manifest

definitions.meaning: surface: a document or a shape; cryptic: also slang for a criminal past, as in 'he has form'
surface: firmly held beliefs; cryptic: findings of guilt in court

explanation.surface: A shape or document in which someone's deeply held beliefs are displayed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Convictions' suggests principles, but it means court verdicts of guilt.
explanation.definitionFit: The official police file lists every offence for which a person has been found guilty.
